THE HEADLINES::

 

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi to participate in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Maharashtra’s Gadchiroli today to mark 151st Birth Anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.
  2. Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer orders special campaign to ensure enrolment of all eligible residents as voters under Special Summary Revision-2027.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra today via video-conferencing. It marks the 151st Birth Anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. Mr Modi will also address the gathering on the occasion.

 

“The Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of 246 development projects worth around three thousand crore rupees. These projects are aimed at strengthening education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities across the country. Besides, Mr Modi will also inaugurate 173 projects, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools for tribal students and 100 Multi-Purpose Centres. Prime Minister will also inaugurate various other projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan. Mr Modi will also inaugurate Tribal Research Institute building at Itanagar, in Arunachal Pradesh and Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum in Mizoram, aimed at preserving tribal culture and heritage. The programme will mark the culmination of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, being observed across the country from 1st to 15th of this month. With Anand and Arzoo, Anupam Mishra, Akashvani News Delhi.”

 

<><><> 

 

The birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda is being also celebrated in Jharkhand today. Our correspondent reports that various programmes, including tribute ceremonies, marches and Deepotsav, are being organised in Ranchi and Ulihatu in Khunti district.

         

“Bhagwan Birsa Munda, the legendary tribal freedom fighter who led the Ulgulan movement against British rule, is being remembered with reverence Ulihatu, his birthplace in Khunti district, is witnessing an atmosphere of enthusiasm and devotion since this morning. The state-level Birsa Festival being organised here is paying tribute to the immortal legacy of Dharti Aaba through traditional dance and music performances and an exhibition of public welfare schemes. Several major programmes are also being organised in the state capital, Ranchi. Meanwhile, the 73-kilometre-long National Tribal Pride March, which began from Ulihatu three days ago, is concluding today at the memorial of Bhagwan Birsa Munda in Kokar, Ranchi. Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar and Chief Minister Hemant Soren, along with several public representatives, are paying tributes to Dharti Aaba. MAHVISH RAHMAN, AKASHVANI NEWS, RANCHI.”

 

<><><> 

         

In Madhya Pradesh, a three day state level event is being held from yesterday to tomorrow on the occasion of Bhagwan Birsa Munda’s birth anniversary. The main state-level programme will be held in Dahi, in Dhar district today.

 

<><><> 

         

President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have paid tributes to Bhagwan Birsa Munda on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, the President said, this day is an opportunity to remember the rich tribal heritage and the historic contributions of tribal communities to the nation.

         

In a social medi post, Mr Modi said, that drawing inspiration from Dharti Aba Bhagwan Birsa Munda, the government is leaving no stone unturned to ensure dignity, opportunity and prosperity for the tribal brothers and sisters.

Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah will perform Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society at a programme to be held in Talegaon Dabhade, at Pune district in Maharashtra today. Mr Shah will also inaugurate the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies and launch Bharat Taxi services for Pune. During the programme, share certificates will also be presented to four Bharat Taxi Sarathis, underscoring the principles of member participation and ownership that lie at the heart of the cooperative model.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa has ordered a special campaign to ensure the enrolment of all eligible state residents as voters under the Special Summary Revision (SSR)-2027. He said campaign days will be held at all 1,73,730 polling stations during November 21-22 and November 28-29 between 10 am and 4 pm. He said those turning 18 on January 1, 2027, will be eligible to apply for enrolment. Advance applications will be accepted from those turning 18 on April 1, July 1 and October 1, 2027. Mr Rinwa said, draft electoral roll, scheduled for publication on November 17, should be provided to all recognised political parties and uploaded on district election websites for public access.

The four day-long Chhath Puja entered its third and main day today, known as Sandhya Arghya. Sandhya Arghya is dedicated to the setting sun. The sacred moment signifies gratitude for the light, warmth, and energy the sun provides throughout the day. Bihar is immersed in the spirit of devotion and celebration as the Chhath Mahaparv reaches its most significant evening ritual today.

 

“Udeti Savita Tamrah, Tamra Evaastameti Cha,
Sampattau Cha Vipattau Cha, Mahatamekarupata.”

“The setting of the Sun is as glorious as its rising. With this spirit of faith and gratitude, devotees across Bihar will offer the first Arghya to the setting Sun today, on the third day of Chhath Mahaparv. In the state capital, Patna, preparations have been completed at various ghats along the Ganga for the evening rituals. Devotees will proceed towards the ghats with traditional bamboo baskets containing fruits, thekua and other offerings. They will offer Arghya to the setting Sun and pray for the prosperity, good health and well-being of their families. Meanwhile, following the Kharna rituals, devotees are observing a 36-hour-long fast without food and water. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has extended Chhath greetings to the people of the country and the state. The state government has made extensive arrangements for the smooth observance of the sacred festival. Savita Pareek, Akashvani News, Patna.”

A well-marked low-pressure area has formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal and is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow evening. India Meteorological Department, IMD has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. Wind speeds reaching up to 60 km per hour are expected over the Andaman Sea, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and large parts of Bay of Bengal. Winds are projected to strengthen up to 80 km per hour over the central Bay of Bengal starting Tuesday. The IMD has advised fishermen currently out at sea to return to the coast immediately and warned against venturing into the Andaman Sea and affected areas of the Bay of Bengal tomorrow.

         

Met Department has also forecast that thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Rajasthan and Uttarakhand today.

The 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits officially began this morning at the Philippine International Convention Centre in Manila. The opening ceremony was presided over by Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., who is chairing this year’s summit as the Philippines holds the ASEAN chairmanship.

 

         

“The three-day summit is being hosted by the Philippines under the theme “Navigating Our Future, Together.” Leaders of ASEAN member countries and dialogue partners are expected to discuss regional security, economic cooperation and other issues of common concern for three days. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Philippines from November 16 to 17 to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. Foreign Affairs experts believe that his participation is expected to provide an opportunity to strengthen India’s Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with ASEAN and explore new areas of cooperation. ASEAN remains an important pillar of India’s Act East Policy, with maritime cooperation, regional connectivity and economic ties forming key areas of engagement. Ishfaq Shah Akashvani News Srinagar.”

Indian-origin business community in the Philippines believes there is significant potential to expand trade and economic cooperation between India and the Philippines. The business leaders see opportunities in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, information technology, renewable energy, infrastructure, manufacturing and agriculture. They believe stronger economic engagement can boost investment, create business partnerships and open new markets for both countries. Talking to Akashvani News, prominent Indian-origin business leader and Chairman of the Philippines-India Business Council, Johnny Chotrani, said bilateral trade reached 3.9 billion US dollars in 2025-26, reflecting the growing economic partnership.

The Indian Panorama section of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 will showcase 25 feature films and 20 non-feature films, highlighting the diversity of contemporary Indian cinema across languages and genres. The feature films have been selected from 404 entries, while the non-feature films were chosen from 358 submissions. ‘Dhurandhar’, directed by Aditya Dhar, has been selected as the opening feature film, while ‘Becoming’, directed by Leena Yadav, will be the opening non-feature film.

In Men’s Cricket, India were 43 for 3 in 10.4 overs against New Zealand in the fifth and final ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, when reports last came in. Earlier, New Zealand won the toss and elected to bowl first.

In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup title in Muscat, Oman, yesterday. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva played sensational knocks to help India snatch victory from the jaws of defeat and successfully chase down a challenging target of 338 runs. Needing three runs off the final delivery, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary to seal India’s record extending ninth title. He remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries and was named player of the match. Aaryavir Sehwag was awarded player of the tournament. Earlier, opting to bat first, Pakistan posted 337 for 9 in their allotted 50 overs.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have congratulated young cricketers for winning Men’s U-19 Asia Cup.

India registered a 2-1 victory over Bhutan in the semifinal yesterday.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, India is moving towards global leadership in emerging technologies, from chips to ships, and from Artificial Intelligence and data centres to quantum computing. He emphasized that reliable power generation is essential to achieving this ambition. Mr Modi said the country is expanding its nuclear power capacity as part of its efforts to achieve clean energy goals and meet its growing energy requirements. The Prime Minister was addressing the gathering  at Bengaluru in Karnataka yesterday, after launching development projects worth over 15,600 crore rupees. Mr Modi said the projects, covering metro, railways and energy infrastructure, will strengthen connectivity, boost economic growth and create new employment opportunities in the state. 

 

 

 

The Prime Minister also inaugurated the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium yesterday evening. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Modi highlighted India’s growing achievements in space science, astronomy and research, saying that the country’s expanding capabilities in these fields are creating new opportunities for young people and contributing to improving life on Earth.  He said the facility will add a new chapter to Mysuru’s contribution to India’s scientific journey and help nurture scientific curiosity among students.

Prime Minister reached Ahmedabad in Gujarat from Karnataka’s Mysuru last evening. He was received at the airport by Gujarat Governor Acharya Devvrat and Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. The Prime Minister subsequently reached Gandhinagar, where he stayed overnight at Lok Bhavan.
         

 

The Prime Minister’s scheduled visit to the Ambaji Temple in Banaskantha district today has been postponed in view of the large number of devotees visiting the shrine during the festive season.
         

 

Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi said, the decision to reschedule the visit was taken to ensure that devotees do not face inconvenience due to security arrangements for the Prime Minister.

The Centre has extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) led by fugitive preacher Dr Zakir Naik for another five years. The Ministry of Home Affairs, declared IRF an unlawful association under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, citing the organisation’s involvement in activities detrimental to the country’s security, communal harmony and secular fabric.
         

 

In a social media post, the Office of Union Home Minister Amit Shah said, the decision reflected the government’s commitment to its policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism and anti-national activities. The post said, the organisation had been involved in activities aimed at inciting communal hatred, promoting terrorism and spreading separatist ideology. More from our correspondent

 

         

 

According to the Home Ministry notification, the government had first declared the Islamic Research Foundation an unlawful association in November, 2016. The ban was subsequently extended in November, 2021. The Ministry said, the IRF had been indulging in activities prejudicial to the security of the country, with the potential to disturb peace and communal harmony and disrupt the secular fabric of the country. The Ministry also cited speeches and statements made by the foundation’s founder and president, Dr Zakir Naik, saying they promoted enmity and hatred among different religious communities and inspired young people belonging to a particular religion, both in India and abroad, to commit terrorist acts. SHIVANG MISRA, AKASHAVNI NEWS, DELHI.

 Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said, India recorded an all-time high in exports, reaching nearly 90 billion dollars in October this year. Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the India International Trade Fair (IITF) in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal said export figure of October comprised around 50 billion dollars in merchandise exports and 40 billion dollars in services exports. He further informed that India’s cumulative exports during the first seven months of the current financial year, up to October, has reached 570 billion dollars. Expressing confidence in the country’s export performance, the Minister said India is well on course to achieve its one-trillion-dollar export target this year.

 

 

 

 

 

The annual India International Trade Fair, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, begins in New Delhi today. It brings together more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad. The theme of this year’s fair is ‘Vikas aur Virasat’. A total of 32 States and Union Territories will participate in the 14-day event, showcasing their regional products, local industries, traditional crafts, cultural heritage, tourism potential and development initiatives.

The festival of Chhath is being observed with religious fervour and devotion across the country, particularly in Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Delhi.

 

 

 On the second day of the four-day festival, devotees will be observing the traditional Kharna ritual today.
         

 

On the occasion, devotees observe a day-long fast, abstaining from both food and water. More from our correspondent:

 

         

 

“Kharna, which signifies purity and sanctity, is an important ritual of the Chhath festival. On this day, devotees observe a day-long fast and perform special prayers in the evening. They then partake of the traditional prasad, which includes jaggery-based kheer, roti and bananas.

 

With this ritual begins the rigorous 36-hour fast, during which devotees abstain from both food and water.

 

Meanwhile, the festive spirit of Chhath is visible across the state, including the capital city of Patna. Traditional Chhath songs have filled the air with devotional fervour. Markets are witnessing brisk sales of bamboo baskets, soop, fruits and earthen stoves, which are essential for the rituals.Savita Pareek, Akashvani News, Patna.”

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has temporarily halted departing flights across the country following a telecommunications failure that affected air traffic control centres, disrupting thousands of flights across the country. According to flight-tracking services, nearly 7,000 flights were delayed or cancelled following the ground stop. The FAA said the communications outage affected all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centres across the United States, prompting the suspension of departures as a precautionary measure.
         

 

Later, the US authorities lifted the nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights and stranded passengers across the country, clearing the way for airlines to resume operations after more than four hours.
         

 

Meanwhile, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said, FAA technicians are investigating the communications failure. Aircraft already in the air were allowed to land, while departing flights were temporarily suspended.

The advisory has been issued following a nationwide ground stop across US airports due to communication outages affecting air traffic operations. The airline has advised passengers to check the latest flight status on its official website and plan their journey to the airport accordingly. Air India said, their teams are closely monitoring the situation and will share the further updates.

The Indian team will be looking to avenge its group-stage defeat against Pakistan and reclaim the continental title after missing out on the trophy in the previous three editions. India will be aiming to clinch a record-extending ninth Under-19 Asia Cup title, while defending champions Pakistan will be looking to lift the trophy for the third time.

India has achieved a significant milestone in its fight against tuberculosis (TB), recording a 38 percent reduction in TB mortality since 2015. This is higher than the global reduction of 35 per cent, reflecting the country’s sustained efforts towards eliminating the disease.

 

India’s reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality highlights the country’s strong performance in reducing TB-related deaths. According to the World Health Organization’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, released yesterday, India has also achieved an impressive 94 per cent treatment success rate among patients suffering from tuberculosis. Health and Family Welfare Ministry said that the progress reflects the impact of intensified interventions under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), including proactive case finding including use of AI enabled X-rays, rapid diagnostics, prompt treatment initiation, differentiated TB care and nutritional support. WITH SHIVANG, NITIKA GUPTA AKASHVANI NEWS DELHI.

India’s premier women’s badminton doubles pair, Treesa Jolly and Pullela Gayatri Gopichand, along with fifteen other sportspersons from various disciplines, will be conferred the Arjuna Award for outstanding performance in Sports and Games. Athletics coach Parveer Singh, boxing coach Chhote Lal Yadav and shooting coach Neha Nandkumar Chavan will be honoured with the Dronacharya Award.

Mr Modi will inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off various development projects worth over 15 thousand 600 crore rupees in Bengaluru this morning. Talking to reporters in Mangaluru last night, Mr Vaishnaw said that the important service will connect coastal Karnataka with Bengaluru.

 

“The 16-coach Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express will comprise Executive Chair coaches and Chair Car coaches, offering passengers a modern and comfortable travel experience. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has proposed reforms to simplify the rules for governing cab rental businesses, promote ease of doing business and strengthen passenger safety. Under the proposed reforms, operators will be allowed to offer cabs with or without drivers. The minimum fleet requirement will be reduced from 50 to five vehicles, with at least 2 cabs per place of operation. The requirement for branches in five tourist cities is removed. The reforms also include a single electronic licence, valid across the State or Union Territory for a uniform fee. Approved places of operation may include airports, stations and bus terminals. It further added that licence grants and renewals have a proposed 60-day timeline. Adding or removing cabs or places of operation has a 30 day deemed-approval mechanism.

The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will be inaugurated at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue.

 

The IITF 2026 is being organised under the theme ‘Vikas aur Virasat’. The fair will host business days from the 14th to 18th of this month, offering opportunities for trade visitors and business-to-business networking. From 19th to 27th November, the fair will open its doors to the general public, families and cultural visitors.

The four-day long Chhath Puja will begin today with the ‘Nahay-Khay’ ritual in different parts of the country. Dedicated to Surya Dev or the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, the festival is observed with strict purity, fasting, and rituals along riverbanks and ghats. The Nahay-Khay’ is marked by ritual bathing and preparation of food while observing strict cleanliness and purity. Traditionally, devotees prepare Kaddubhaat as prasad, marking the beginning of the four-day festival.

 

The second day will be observed as ‘Kharna’. Devotees will observe a day-long fast and break it in the evening after offering prayers and consuming prasad. This will be followed by the rigorous ‘nirjala’ fast.
On the third day, devotees will gather at rivers, ponds and other Chhath ghats in the evening to worship Chhathi Maiya and offer ‘arghya’ to the setting sun.

The festival will conclude on Monday morning with devotees offering ‘arghya’ to the rising sun.

In a social media post, Mr Modi said that today marks Nahay-Khay, the first day of the festival. He extended his greetings to all devotees observing the fast and wished that everyone receives the blessings of Chhathi Maiya.

The countdown to the 57th International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026, begins in Goa today, with the curtain raiser press conference scheduled this morning. The nine-day festival will be held from November 20 to 28 in Goa. Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant will grace the curtain raiser programme.

Leaders, scientists, civil society representatives, activists and others from nearly 200 countries, including India, are gathering for two weeks in Turkey’s Mediterranean resort city of Antalya for the 31st Conference of Parties to the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), beginning today, with aim to accelerate clean energy, scale up climate finance and strengthen resilience. The summit will continue till November 20.

The Conference of the Parties (COP), the highest-level global climate summit held annually under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), is bringing together heads of state, Ministers, scientists, business leaders, and civil society representatives from around the world and serves as the primary platform for negotiating and advancing collective action to combat climate change. At COP31, the World Metrological Organisation (WMO) will support countries by providing authoritative scientific observations and information on the state of the global climate system, including through the launch of its flagship State of Climate update 2026, a science-based annual assessment of climate indicators and impacts.
